shortTheory.question: State Hooke’s law.
shortTheory.answer: If a force F is applied on a spring to stretch or compress it, the extension or compression x has been found directly proportional to the applied force within the elastic limit.

shortTheory.question: Define density.
shortTheory.answer: Density of a substance is defined as its mass per unit volume.

shortTheory.question: Define pressure.
shortTheory.answer: Pressure is defined as the force exerted normally on unit area of an object.

shortTheory.question: State Pascal’s law.
shortTheory.answer: When pressure is applied at one point in an enclosed fluid, it is transmitted equally to all parts of fluid without loss.

shortTheory.question: Why is it painful to walk bare footed on pebbles?
shortTheory.answer: But when we walk on pebbles, the contact area is reduced. Then the pressure due to reaction force becomes so high that it becomes painful.

shortTheory.question: What is the relationship between liquid pressure and the depth of the liquid?
shortTheory.answer: Equation 6.4 shows that pressure in a liquid increases with depth. The value of pressure depends on the depth and density of the liquid.

definitions.text: Such a force is known as deforming force.
An object is said to be elastic, if after removal of the deforming force, it restores to its original size and shape.
This property of the material is known as elasticity.
Some materials such as clay dough or plasticine do not return to their original shape after the removal of the deforming force. They are known as inelastic materials.
Most of the materials are elastic up to a certain limit known as elastic limit.
If a force F is applied on a spring to stretch or compress it, the extension or compression x has been found directly proportional to the applied force within the elastic limit.
Density of a substance is defined as its mass per unit volume.
Pressure is defined as the force exerted normally on unit area of an object.
This force per unit area is the atmospheric pressure.
Instruments which measure the atmospheric pressure are called barometers.
When pressure is applied at one point in an enclosed fluid, it is transmitted equally to all parts of fluid without loss.

fullMarks: For a definition or law, write the complete statement clearly; for Pascal’s law include both “enclosed fluid” and “equally … without loss.”
For a numerical, write the given quantities first and convert them to SI units before substituting: cm to m, cm² to m², litres to m³, and g to kg.
Show the formula, substitution with units, calculation, and final answer with its SI unit. Keep suitable significant figures.
For spring questions, use extension x (not the spring’s full length) and show that the force–extension relationship applies only within the elastic limit.
For pressure questions, identify the area actually in contact and use the area perpendicular to the normal force. For maximum and minimum pressure, use the smallest and largest faces respectively.
For liquid pressure, state that it depends on liquid density and depth, then use P = ρgh. Do not include atmospheric pressure unless the question asks for total pressure.
For hydraulic systems, show equal pressure at both pistons before calculating the unknown force; label the small and large piston areas correctly.
In an explanation of hydraulic brakes, describe the pressure transfer through the brake fluid and how the pistons press the brake pads against the discs or drums.

mistakes: Using the spring’s total length instead of its extension. Fix: calculate extension as the change in length, then use k = F ÷ x.
Leaving extensions, dimensions, or areas in cm or cm² in an SI calculation. Fix: convert lengths to m and areas to m² before substituting.
Using mass in place of force when finding pressure. Fix: first find weight using F = mg, then use P = F ÷ A.
Choosing the wrong face of a brick for maximum or minimum pressure. Fix: the smallest contact area gives maximum pressure; the largest gives minimum pressure.
Thinking liquid pressure depends on the container’s shape or the area of its base. Fix: for pressure at a depth, use P = ρgh; it depends on density, depth, and g.
Swapping the small and large piston areas in a hydraulic calculation. Fix: label A₁ and A₂ carefully and use F₁ ÷ A₁ = F₂ ÷ A₂.

Writing that pressure is transmitted equally by any fluid without mentioning confinement. Fix: state that pressure applied at one point in an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally to all parts without loss.
